what_it_is: The evidence discipline: attach handles that resolve — comment IDs as working links, SHAs of real commits, file:line pairs that exist at the cited ref. Resolve every handle against the live tree at the cited ref before you count it. Lead with the label — what the thing IS, what it DOES, why it MATTERS — and put the identifier last, as the quiet proof of the sentence above it.
what_it_does: Makes every claim checkable by a stranger in one command, with no questions. A dead handle is a defect in the verdict, not a formatting nit — it means the claim underneath it was never verified.
why_it_matters: The authoring repair: check_pr_receipt.py went from 2 dead handles to 11 live / 0 dead at the pushed head — the branch name de-backticked and given a live tree URL, full repo paths used, the PR body's ## Evidence re-pinned to the new head. The receipt gate went PASS on the repaired handles, not on promises. The lesson in the machinery: the fix belonged to the body's handles, never to the gate. The opposite: Judge's scorecard on #2566 — NEEDS_WORK at 8.5/10 — named 4 dead handles: two hidden_files/ paths absent from the repo at tip (byte-verified zero entries), one branch name used as a file path, one machine-local path (receipt: comment 6161777038). And #2592's receipt-gate FAILURE on path:operations-manual-2026-10-14-v2.md — goal-workspace filenames are not repo-resolvable paths (comment 6172427473). In both cases the handles were the work: fix the body, never weaken the gate.
key_rules: Every claim carries evidence a stranger can re-derive in one command. Every handle resolves at the cited ref, or it is not evidence.
Lead with the label — what the thing IS, what it DOES, why it MATTERS — and put the identifier last, as the quiet proof of the sentence above it.
Resolve every handle against the live tree at the cited ref BEFORE you count it.
A dead handle is a defect in the verdict, not a formatting nit — it means the claim underneath was never verified.
If the gate fired, re-run its matcher against the live bytes before judging it. The fix belongs to the body's handles, never to the gate.
Memory is rumor. If you can't open the handle, mark the claim UNVERIFIED — not 'probably fine.'
No bare backticked identifiers. Every identifier rides a plain-words sentence.
test: Does every handle resolve at the cited ref?
Could a stranger re-derive my claim from my links alone — one command, no questions?
Did I lead with the label (what it is) and put the number last?
Is every identifier attached to a plain-words sentence that explains it?
If the gate fired, did I re-run its matcher against the live bytes before judging it?

enforcement.real: The receipt gate (check_pr_receipt.py — refuses unresolvable handles; a gate that fires correctly is not a false negative). The L339 handle-resolution rule (a scorecard resolves every handle before counting it). The L387 rule: before calling a gate failure a false negative, re-run the gate's matcher against live body bytes — the fix belongs to the body's handles, never to the gate. The gate grammar: no bare backticked identifiers.
enforcement.proposed: No compile-time handle checker exists — resolution is verified by hand and by the receipt gate at merge time, not by a linter. Nothing additional is proposed for this area beyond the machinery above.
